backend_config._cell_backend_note: Cells are tagged with the backend family ('vllm'), not the deployment name. This key lets a second vLLM deployment select the same matrix without duplicating 79 cells. Results still land in results/vllm-120b/ because the run directory uses the deployment name.
backend_config._tokenizer_note: tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, special_tokens_map.json and chat_template.jinja are byte-identical between the 20B and 120B snapshots (verified 2026-08-18 by sha256). The prepared datasets were bucket-sliced with the 20B tokenizer and are therefore valid here without regeneration; this path points at the 120B snapshot for provenance only.
backend_config.deployment: vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:928dde7d6c19478c9c6ab975fed12e6466f6d9b7cb3695d218e287c0c88ad608 (same image as the 20B campaign); GPT-OSS-120B HF revision b5c939de, quantization mxfp4 via MARLIN MoE backend, TRITON_ATTN; max-model-len=65536, max-num-seqs set per campaign via start_vllm_120b.sh; gpu-memory-utilization=0.85 measured 33.07-35.25 GiB KV pool / 904670-964375 tokens across two identical launches, so the pool varies ~6% run to run because the unified memory is shared with a graphical desktop -- pin it with --kv-cache-memory before the formal campaign. The reported 'maximum concurrency 13.80x' is 904670/65536 and only binds on full-length requests; the whole 79-cell matrix fits, the heaviest cell being rag-*-b016k-c32 at ~532K tokens. Weights+non-torch 66.68 GiB, cold load ~9.7 min.
backend_config._url_note: start_vllm_120b.sh publishes the container's 8000 on host 18001 so it cannot be confused with the 20B deployment on 18000. The DFlash variant uses 18002.

campaign_config.name: gpt-oss-20b-dataset-v1-dgx
campaign_config.description: DGX Spark (GB10 Grace Blackwell, ARM64) llama.cpp vs vLLM A/B; shares the RTX 4090 matrix, seed, durations and stability limits so both backends stay comparable across hardware
campaign_config._gpu_idle_utilization_pct_note: RTX 4090 reference used 5. Raised to 12 on DGX Spark: this host runs a graphical desktop (gnome-remote-desktop-daemon holds the GPU) and an idle vLLM EngineCore still polls, so measured idle utilisation floors at 7-8% and the strict '< threshold' test at line 160 of run_benchmarks.py could never pass. Working utilisation is 94%, so 12 still separates busy from idle. This gates when a run may start; it does not affect what is measured.
